correctness.rationale: For every tuple, powers of all forward weights define an acyclic index graph. The recurrence for its maximum path weight is proved inductively. The nonnegative potential increments yield an explicit real Cho certificate of cost equal to the maximum subsequence cost; the reverse inclusion is the sum of disjoint interval bounds. Boundary arguments separately address the maximum product, infinite weights, degree zero and infinite scales. The complete six-edge paper example is checked explicitly. The self-contained code verified 1510 finite tuples and an additional numerical 1800 tuples; experiments are corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected all-graph nerve (Cho 2019) has no monoidal Rips comparison; the metric comparison (Ivanov–Xu 2024, Proposition 2.6) is explicitly metric-only, although its proof is close and could be generalized; the 2025/2026 monoidal Rips paper explicitly claims strictness for +_2 on a directed network, which the exhibited admissible radius-four parameters refute. The new directed theorem states the stronger generality and gives an \(O(n^2)\) exact formula rather than merely rephrasing the metric statement. None of the queried published mathematical research records covered this exact correction or result.

value.rationale: The result resolves a published claimed structural separation of two widely used persistent simplicial set constructions on arbitrary directed networks. The all-exponents interval-certificate formula is a constructive \(O(n^2)\) alternative to exponential subsequence tests or an existential optimization, and it pinpoints why a specific published counterexample cannot witness strictness. It does not make an unsupported claim for all monoidal lattices.
